management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Corneal Abrasion of the right eye, superficial epithelial defect
Perform fluorescein staining under cobalt blue light (visualize green epithelial scratch, confirm no infiltrate)
Provide topical erythromycin ointment and oral analgesia; consider a short-course cycloplegic only for clinically significant traumatic iritis or photophobia
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Corneal Abrasion of the right eye, superficial epithelial defect.
reference_soap.plan: Check visual acuity, pupil shape/reactivity, and fluorescein staining under cobalt-blue light to identify an epithelial defect and exclude an infiltrate. Provide topical erythromycin ointment and oral analgesia; consider a short-course cycloplegic only for clinically significant traumatic iritis or photophobia. Do not patch. It happened about two hours ago while we were playing on the floor in the living room.
It is only in my right eye; my left eye feels completely normal.
The pain is severe, about an eight out of ten, and it feels like a constant sharp burning and scratching sensation.
Yes, it feels exactly like a piece of grit or sand is trapped under my eyelid every time I blink.
The whole white of my right eye turned red right after it happened, especially around the colored part.
It looks a bit blurry because my eye keeps filling up with tears, but when I wipe them away my actual vision seems okay.
Yes, light really hurts and makes my eye throb, so I have to keep it clamped shut in bright areas.
No, I haven't seen any colored halos or rings around lights, and I don't have a headache or feel sick to my stomach.
It has just been clear, watery tears streaming down constantly; there is no thick yellowish pus or sticky crust.
No, it doesn't itch at all; it just burns and hurts.
My eyelid feels a little swollen from all the tearing and squinting, but there are no painful bumps or crusty rims on the lid.
Blinking is very painful because of the scratching, but moving my eye deep in the socket doesn't cause any extra ache.
No, I am not seeing double at all.
No, I feel fine otherwise and haven't had any fever, chills, or body aches.
No, I haven't had a cold, sore throat, or cough, and nobody around me at home or work has an eye infection.
No, I have never worn contact lenses or glasses; my eyesight has always been good.
It was just my toddler's little fingernail poking me; no metal, wood shavings, glass, or chemicals got into my eye.
No, I don't suffer from seasonal allergies, hay fever, asthma, or eczema.
I work on a computer at the office, but I've never had dry eyes or dry mouth issues before today.
No, I don't have any morning back stiffness, swollen joints, mouth sores, or bowel trouble.
No, I have never had cold sores, shingles, or any rash or blisters on my face or forehead.
No, I don't take blood thinners, and I haven't had any heavy coughing, vomiting, or straining.
I have never had eye surgery, glaucoma, cataracts, or any serious eye problems in the past.
I think his fingernail must have scratched or scraped the surface of my eyeball.
I'm in a lot of misery with this pain and watering, so I was hoping you could examine it and give me numbing drops or medication to relieve the pain.
I have no past medical illnesses, high blood pressure, or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter painkillers, or eye drops.
I do not have any allergies to medications or latex.

exam.finding: The patient appears in moderate distress, holding a tissue over his right eye and squinting with noticeable blepharospasm and tearing.
Blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg, heart rate 74 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, and temperature 36.6 °C.
The right eye demonstrates diffuse conjunctival and ciliary injection with clear lacrimation and no subconjunctival hemorrhage; the left eye is clear and quiet.

Visual acuity is 20/25 in the right eye (improving after blinking) and 20/20 in the left eye; pupils are equal, round, and reactive; fluorescein staining under cobalt-blue light reveals a 4 x 2 mm linear corneal epithelial defect on the right eye with no stromal infiltrate and a negative Seidel test; upper eyelid eversion shows no retained foreign body.
Periorbital and facial skin is intact with no erythema, edema, vesicular lesions, or bruising.
Extraocular eye movements are full in both eyes without diplopia, and facial sensation across all trigeminal branches is intact.
